Preserve the actual surrounding photograph as closely as possible; register to the three landmarks: the dark metal hoops completely beyond the grass on the upper left, the dark pot and wooden bed across the grass on the right, and the two pale single paths leading from the bottom of the picture to the crosswise grass strip. Crop remains wide landscape 5:3. This first image alone sets the location. The other references supply only the real man's working pose and likeness. Do not introduce a shed from the pose reference.

Remove only the black sheeting, its weights and spent crop in the CENTRAL foreground bed BETWEEN those two single brick paths. Keep the black sheeting on the adjoining bed to the left and all neighbouring structures in place. Make several young, plausibly spaced brassica transplants in the CENTRAL bed. Place ONE small low rectangular cane netting frame in the very CENTRE of that bed, centred across its width between the paths and set inward from the grassy end. The viewer must see a generous strip of bare earth beyond every foot, including both front posts. Its two long sides run AWAY from the camera in the SAME direction as the two converging brick paths, not across the bed or path. A practical two-bay frame sized for a few plants: six slim weathered bamboo legs, asymmetrically weathered real used yellow-green tennis balls about 6.7cm in diameter at the six joints (four corners and two midpoint supports), four perimeter top rails AND a crossrail at the midpoints. Rails join snug holes in balls; smooth rounded balls cap the uprights, no tips poke out. Keep plenty of room above the plants; leave the frame uncovered so each joint and feet are clear. There is visible garden soil on BOTH sides of it between supports and bricks. Keep the entire frame comfortably inside the picture, especially lower feet. The scale of its rear end must allow John to reach it.

CRITICAL layout: the grass path in photo 1 forms a continuous mown band left to right behind the bed. Preserve its original inner and outer edges, original width, surface and perspective. It has NO vegetables or tall plants, no added soil and no cane feet. Keep the existing two brick finger paths visible on BOTH sides of the demonstration bed. Do not invent edging boards or turn the foreground into turf. Do not widen the soil boundaries to fit the frame. Reduce the frame to fit within the earth. The black covered bed on left and the wooden structure in distant background are the neighbouring areas.

Keep John kneeling close to his original place, across the far end, head turned and inclined to the left looking at the work. He is pressing a horizontal cane into a tennis ball at the end within his natural reach, with his other hand steadying the ball. Preserve his moss-green knitted hat, teal fleece, sweater and jeans, his usual small chin tucked back behind the lower lip as seen in the two photographic face references, grey beard following the short slope back towards collar. Keep appearance, face size and body proportions from the real photo. The technique and his hands must read at small book size. Natural candid gardening photograph, real April daylight, a close enough view of hands and frame to read. No inset, no text, no lines or markings.
